elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement to an Affiliate without IBM's consent.
elements.evidence: The exception expressly permits Customer to assign the Agreement “to an Affiliate” notwithstanding the general consent requirement.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without IBM's consent to a successor organization by merger.
elements.evidence: The consent-free exception covers assignment “to a successor organization by merger.”

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without IBM's consent to a successor organization by acquisition.
elements.evidence: The consent-free exception covers assignment “to a successor organization by ... acquisition.”

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without IBM's consent to a successor organization through a sale of substantially all assets.
elements.evidence: The consent-free exception covers assignment to a successor organization through a “sale of substantially all assets.”

elements.element: IBM may not assign this Agreement without Customer's prior consent.
elements.evidence: The clause states, “IBM will not assign this Agreement without Customer's prior written consent.”

elements.element: Customer's consent to an IBM assignment may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: IBM's assignment restriction states that Customer's consent is “not to be unreasonably withheld.”

elements.element: IBM may never assign this Agreement to a competitor of Customer.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly provides that IBM “will not assign to a competitor of Customer.”

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives IBM no right to terminate this Agreement.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly states, “Customer's change of control gives IBM no right to terminate this Agreement.”

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement to a successor without IBM's consent.
elements.evidence: Customer may assign without consent to a successor organization by merger, consolidation, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets.

elements.element: Customer must give IBM written notice of an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: No written-notice obligation applies to Customer's consent-free successor assignments.

elements.element: IBM may assign this Agreement to a successor without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: IBM cannot make any assignment, including an assignment to a successor, without Customer's prior written consent.

elements.element: IBM must give Customer written notice of an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no written-notice mechanism for an IBM successor assignment; requiring prior written consent is not an express written-notice right.

elements.element: Customer assignments other than successor assignments require IBM's consent.
elements.evidence: Customer may assign to an Affiliate without consent, even where that Affiliate is not a successor.

elements.element: IBM may not unreasonably withhold consent to Customer assignments for which consent is required.
elements.evidence: The general Customer assignment restriction requires IBM's prior written consent and states that such consent is “not to be unreasonably withheld.”

elements.element: IBM assignments other than successor assignments require Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: The clause requires Customer's prior written consent for every IBM assignment, which includes all non-successor assignments.

elements.element: Customer may not unreasonably withhold consent to IBM assignments for which consent is required.
elements.evidence: The IBM assignment restriction expressly states that Customer's consent is “not to be unreasonably withheld.”

result.reason: The operative language fully implements the preferred position: Customer receives the specified consent-free assignment rights, IBM is subject to Customer consent and an absolute competitor prohibition, and IBM has no termination right upon Customer's change of control. The fallback is not independently satisfied because neither party has the specified written-notice framework, IBM lacks a consent-free successor-assignment right, and Customer's Affiliate carveout extends beyond successor assignments. The redline is otherwise targeted and leaves unrelated existing terms, including Customer's continuing liability after assignment, unchanged.
